title: Nvidia buys stakes in French tech startups Doctolib, Genesis AI
source_used: Trending Topics (reads Nvidia blog post and Les Echos); Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401)
key_facts: Nvidia announced, in a blog post about its France activities, investments in four French companies: Doctolib, Genesis AI, Pigment and Entalpic.
Neither Nvidia nor the start-ups disclosed amounts or stake sizes; Les Echos says they are minority stakes.
Jensen Huang announced the deals at a reception on Place Vendome attended by French economy minister Roland Lescure.

Doctolib (medical appointments, valued at EUR 5.8 billion in 2022) is building AI agents for doctors; Genesis AI (Paris and Bay Area) builds foundation models for general-purpose robots; Pigment is planning software; Entalpic uses AI to design materials.
Nvidia says it has committed nearly $10 billion to Europe's tech ecosystem and plans another $2 billion of European deals within a week, The Next Web reported (via Trending Topics).
Huang: "Europe needs to get in the race"; he favours open AI models as cheaper and more adaptable.

Critics call Nvidia's investments circular financing (investees use the money to buy Nvidia chips); Huang rejects this, saying the stakes are small relative to the business and each stands on its own merits.
quote_evidence: Jensen Huang brought his checkbook to Paris: Nvidia is investing in four French tech companies, including the health care scale-up Doctolib.
Neither Nvidia nor the start-ups disclosed how much money is involved or how large the stakes are.
According to Les Echos, they are minority stakes.
why_it_matters_hint: Nvidia is spreading stakes across French health, robotics, software and materials start-ups during a European tour, while critics question the circularity.
notes: Reuters original blocked (HTTP 401); France 24 (AFP) blocked; read Trending Topics, which relays Nvidia's blog post and Les Echos. Reuters headline: "Nvidia buys stakes in French tech startups Doctolib, Genesis AI". Yahoo Finance headline attributes the first report to Les Echos.
